title: GPU pool noisy-neighbor isolation & experiment log
content:
Summary:

This is an on-call investigation log + experiment notebook for a recurring tail-latency regression affecting a subset of the Dedicated GPU pool (pool: ded-gpu-v2-europe-west). Symptoms first seen as increased 99th-percentile token latency for text-generation routes between 2025-09-12 and 2025-09-16. Root suspicion: noisy neighbors interacting with autoscaler cooldowns + MIG partitioning causing intermittent GPU saturation and cross-tenant KV cache thrash.

Why this doc exists:
- capture the ad-hoc isolation tests we ran (commands, results)
- document hypotheses that were validated/invalidated
- draft runbook addenda for noisy-neighbor triage for Dedicated pools
- list follow-up engineering tasks and owners

Timeline (quick):
- 2025-09-12 02:14 UTC: Alert SRE-High - route gen-prod-eu > latency_99 > 600ms for >10m
- 2025-09-12 02:30 UTC: Oncall (Lena) starts triage, confirms spike across 3 nodes in pool
- 2025-09-12 03:00 UTC: Short-term mitigation: shift ~25% of traffic to fallback model variant (lower perf requirement) to relieve load
- 2025-09-13 11:00 UTC: Cluster-autoscaler observed delayed scale-up due to cooldown=10m with bursty request pattern -> scaling step stalled
- 2025-09-14 08:45 UTC: Experiment 1: live-migrate suspect pods to spare nodes to test affinity impact
- 2025-09-15 09:20 UTC: Experiment 2: apply soft QoS limits (cgroup/gpu scheduler weight) to top noisy tenants
- 2025-09-16 21:00 UTC: Confirmed correlation with a particular tenant job type (batch-long-running inference) that didn't declare expected resource hints

Observations and signals checked (ordered):
- Alerts: SLO latency, capacity saturation, GPU memory pressure alerts
- Metrics: node_gpu_utilization, kernel_latency_distribution, rpc_queue_depth, model_kv_cache_hit_rate
- PromQL examples used (quick copy):
  - avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization[5m]) by (node) > 0.8
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - sum(kv_cache_hits) / sum(kv_cache_requests) by (model, node)
- Traces: spike correlated with queuing before serving container, not model compute time (compute p95 stable, p99 queued)
- Logs: CUDA driver warnings around memory allocation retry on two nodes (node-13, node-14)

Hypotheses (initial):
1) Noisy neighbor: a long-running batch job absent resource limits (or mismatched MIG) causes kernel-level contention that impacts co-located pods.
2) Autoscaler mis-config: cooldowns + step-sizes too conservative for bursty request distributions, leading to sustained queuing until scale completes.
3) Prefix cache thrash: KV cache was being invalidated across model variants due to mixed-tenant routing and model-level cache sharing, increasing compute I/O and mem pressure.

Experiments and results:
- Experiment A: Forced pod isolation (cordon + drain + schedule target pods onto dedicated spare nodes)
  - Command snippet used: kubectl cordon node-08; kubectl drain node-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  - Result: Latency returned to baseline on nodes that were isolated; two suspect nodes still showed intermittent spikes. Conclusion: co-location plays role but not sole cause.

- Experiment B: Adjust autoscaler cooldown and step-size for pool ded-gpu-v2-europe-west to cooldown=60s, step-size=+25%
  - Observed: Faster scale-up removed sustained queuing for short bursts, but cost increased unexpectedly for noise periods when traffic had multiple small spikes. Conclusion: autoscale tuning reduces tail latency but increases churn/cost; need smarter policy (predictive/burst detection).

- Experiment C: Soft QoS limits via nvidia-smi application clocks? No - requires privileged access. Instead we tested container-level env hint enforcement + MIG re-assignment for suspicious tenants (migrate pod to MIG partitioned node).
  - Result: When the batch job was placed on a node with smaller MIG slices (exclusive to it), neighbor pods improved. Strong evidence that improper MIG partitioning contributed.

Key evidence that led to conclusions:
- GPU compute time distribution remained stable while queue time increased -> queuing, not model slowdown
- Two nodes had repeated driver WARN allocation loops aligned with suspect tenant's run times
- The batch job did not set the resource annotation model/gpu-intent or requested too large ephemeral memory; scheduler placed it on shared partition
- Autoscaler logs: SCA-logs show delayed scale up because pod request patterns fell into 'burst' window that was below scale target threshold; cooldown prevented rapid subsequent steps

Short-term mitigations applied (and their status):
- Traffic shift to fallback variant (applied 2x in windows of 10m) — status: temporary mitigation, rolled back 2025-09-13 14:00 UTC
- Tightened admission checks for batch jobs in the pool: require resource_hint: mig:exclusive or request >=X GPU-mig slices — status: applied as policy (PR referencing below), still monitoring
- Temporary autoscaler override during peak hours: allowed quicker step-outs for the pool — status: reverted after cost analysis

Runbook draft additions (items to add to /confluence/gpu-pool-observability-playbook):
- Quick triage checklist for noisy-neighbor in Dedicated pools:
  1) Check node_gpu_utilization and kernel_latency for nodes in the pool
  2) Identify top 3 pods by gpu_utilization (prom query) and inspect pod resource annotations
  3) If driver WARNs present, isolate node and migrate pods to spares
  4) Check autoscaler events (kubectl get hpa/ssa events) for cooldown-related delays
  5) If KV cache hit_rate < 80% and high queuing, consider increasing cache TTL for the model and route traffic to cached nodes
  6) Escalate to infra (annotate node with noisy-neighbor and schedule maintenance)
- Log templates: include PromQL snippets and kubectl commands (see appendix)
- Owner mapping: who to page when kernel WARNs vs scheduler mis-placement detected (infra vs platform-eng)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did driver allocation retry appear specifically on node-13 and node-14? Hardware flake? kernel driver mismatch?
- How to automate detection of 'batch jobs without resource hints' at admission time without generating false positives for long-running lightweight workloads?
- What's the appropriate autoscale policy for bursty latency-sensitive routes vs batch-backed background traffic?

Follow-ups and action items (with tentative owners and ETA):
- SRE: add automated Prometheus alert that flags 'mixed-MIG occupancy' patterns (owner: Ben Cho) - ETA 2025-10-09
- Platform: admission controller check for required gpu resource_hint for Dedicated pools (owner: Aisha Patel) - ETA 2025-10-02 (in progress)
- Infra: audit node images on node-13/node-14 and schedule driver upgrade if needed (owner: Marco Ruiz) - ETA 2025-09-26 (done)
- Product/Cost: define autoscale policy experiments with simulated workloads to measure cost vs latency trade-offs (owner: Sofia Nguyen) - ETA 2025-10-16
- Eng-Serving-runtime: investigate KV cache isolation per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant thrash (owner: TBD) - ETA 2025-11-01

Appendix (commands & quick queries):
- List top GPU users: kubectl top pods --containers | grep gpu || kubectl get pods -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests, GPU:.metadata.annotations
- PromQL snippets:
  - topk(5, sum by(pod) (rate(gpu_utilization_seconds_total[5m])))
  - sum by(node) (avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization[5m]))
  - rate(inference_requests_total[1m]) by (route)
- Check autoscaler events: kubectl describe hpa ded-gpu-v2 --namespace=inference | sed -n '/Events:/,$p'
- Node driver logs: sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 500 --no-pager

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- might implement a light-weight 'niceness' score for pods feeding into scheduler to avoid pure first-come-first-serve on shared partitions
- consider a short-lived per-tenant MIG carve-out for heavy batch windows (cron + migrate) as temporary policy
- add a small echo traffic generator to detect noisy neighbors proactively (cheap periodic probe)

Incidental links and references:
- Incident ticket: INC-1842
- Autoscaler experiment PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/pull/87
- Confluence draft for playbook: confluence:gpu-pool-observability-playbook

Last thoughts:
This incident is multi-factor: no single quick fix. Best path forward is layered: admission-time guardrails + smarter autoscale policies + targeted MIG isolation for predictable batch jobs. The runbook addenda will aim to shorten time-to-isolation from ~45m to <10m for future incidents.

-- Lena
(edited by Marco, Aisha, Sofia 2025-09-30)
